learning_outcomes.text: Demonstrate the capacity for analysis and synthesis.
Demonstrate skills for organization, planning, and strategy.
Acquire the capacity for effective problem-solving.
Express oneself correctly in Spanish, both orally and in writing.
Acquire skills related to the use of computer programs for calculation, data analysis, and processing within their field of application.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.
Acquire the capacity for autonomous learning and concern for knowledge and continuous training.
Motivation for quality and continuous improvement.

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering, and aptitude to apply knowledge on: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.

syllabus_topics: Successive extensions of the concept of number. Topological definitions on the real line. The absolute value.
Real functions of a real variable
First definitions. Limits, properties. Continuity, properties. Theorems on continuous functions.
First definitions. Theorems on differentiable functions. Graphical representation of functions.
Definition of primitive. The indefinite integral: Properties. Calculation of primitives.

Integrable function in an interval [a,b]: The definite integral. Mean Value Theorems, Fundamental Theorem of Integral Calculus and Barrow's rule. Improper integrals of 1st and 2nd kind. Convergent, divergent and oscillating improper integrals. Applications to the calculation of areas, lengths and volumes.
Definitions. Convergence criteria. Sum of numerical series.
Functional series: Definitions. Power series. Power series expansion of certain functions.
teaching_methods: Theory classes and problem solving using blackboard and/or projector
Practicals with the help of computer software
Individual or group tutorials on student request

assessment_methods.method: Written exam of theory, questions, and problems from the first part of the course
Written exam of theory, questions, and problems from the second part of the course

assessment_rules: The weighted average of the three procedures must be at least 5 out of 10 points to pass the course. A minimum of 4 out of 10 is required for each written exam, and a minimum of 3.5 out of 10 is required for the computer-based problem-solving tests. Fraudulent performance in any assessment test will result in a zero grade for the corresponding procedure, without prejudice to disciplinary action.
